messages:
amanda: Quick Q re: /v1/rerank tie handling — do we keep stable ordering by input order when scores equal or introduce deterministic id-based tie-break? Need for compatibility with downstream deduping.
josh: We currently return array in rank order but don't guarantee stable ties. Clients complained when results shuffled after change. :grimacing:
lia: Suggest adding explicit tie_break param with default 'stable' to preserve current behavior. Example: "tie_break": "stable|id|shuffle". Also add 'rank' integer field so clients can rely on explicit positions.
patrick: If default is 'stable' we must also define what 'stable' means — preserve client's input order after scoring. Good.
kevin: Also propose normalizing scores to [0,1] and include raw_score to aid debugging. Backcompat: adding fields is ok; changing score semantics is not.
amanda: draft schema snippet:
```json
{"items": [{"id": "string", "score": "number"}], "tie_break": "string (optional)"}
```
lia: nit: call the returned score 'score' (normalized) and add 'raw_score' (model logit) optional.
josh: how about tie resolution: when tie_break='id' do we use lexicographic id? stable but deterministic. good for A/B tests.
patrick: edge case: null scores (e.g., item skipped) — we should define null => treat as -inf so they sink to bottom. agree?
kevin: yep, treat null as -inf and include note in changelog. Also add 'tie_seed' optional int for shuffle to be deterministic.
amanda: OK I'll open a PR with schema + migration notes. tagging @josh @lia for review. deadline EOD tomorrow.
josh: ack, will review tomorrow morning.
rerank-bot: Deploy plan: add feature-flag 'rerank.tie_break' and rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100% across dedicated clusters. Doc link: https://redwood.internal/docs/rerank/tie-break
lia: small follow-up: add tests — deterministic ordering tests + null-score cases + tie_seed consistency.
amanda: thanks all :thumbsup:
